rules.name: executable bits
rules.why: Windows has no executable bit. A case that gives a file one with chmod, or takes one away, measures Cygwin's imitation of it when bash passes, and a native shell has nothing to read.

rules.name: symbolic links
rules.why: Making a symbolic link on Windows takes a privilege an ordinary user does not have, and CI's does not either.

rules.name: resource limits
rules.why: Windows has no resource limits for ulimit to read or set. nemosh refuses ulimit there, as docs/support-matrix.md says, and bash's answers come from Cygwin's imitation.

rules.name: descriptors past 2
rules.why: A Windows program is handed no descriptor past 2, so read_from_fd.py cannot read the one a case opened for it, whichever shell opened it.

rules.name: HOME
rules.why: The harness sets HOME to each case's own directory, where Oils leaves it unset: on Windows every shell measured here would otherwise take the user's profile for it, and a case that wrote under ~ would write into the user's real home.
